acceptance: forge-runtime tests: anon WS mux and SSE subscribe to a private table are refused (WS error frame; SSE 401 + Bearer challenge, not text/event-stream).
The same tests: anon subscribe to a literal-predicate (anon-readable) table streams over both transports.
forge-portal-e2e P2.2 and the realtime-sse anon-refusal spec target a private table, fail on the dev stack before and pass after, run output in evidence.
author: rory

gaps.description: Diffed the roadmap step IP-1 (title, notes, three acceptance lines) against the recorded intent statement: the intent names both transports, the refusal shape for each, and the anon-readable control case, and names the dev-stack e2e evidence

The step acceptance says WebSocket "closed or rejected before any frame" but multi-protocol.spec.ts:140 requires an `error` frame and no `subscribed`; the intent reads rejection as an error frame with no subscribed/event frame
gaps.note: the mux upgrade is per-op auth by design (the spec comment says so) and the e2e that must go green asserts an error frame, so closing the socket would fail the very spec the step names

gaps.description: The step premise (a runtime hole) was false: forge-storage crud_emitter.rs:64-90,374-391 makes a literal-predicate select policy publicly readable, and probe_items has carried one since forge-portal-e2e b906f9b (PS-1). Amended the roadmap step: scope and lands now include forge-portal-e2e, and the fail-before criterion moved to the e2e specs, which are red today
The forge-runtime tests cannot fail before a fix, because nothing in the runtime is wrong; they pin an enforced contract that had no WS-mux anonymous coverage at all
gaps.note: inventing a runtime defect to satisfy the original wording would ship a change that refuses anonymous reads of public tables, which the documented literal-policy design (docs row-security: serve published rows to logged-out visitors) requires

gaps.description: Diffed the plan (retarget the e2e specs to probe_locked; add tests/realtime_anon_subscribe.rs) against intent revision 2. Its second criterion, an anonymous subscribe to a literal-policy table streams over BOTH transports, is not met by the tree: ip1-rt-tests ran 3 pass and 1 fail. anon_ws_subscribe_to_a_public_table_streams gets subscribed and then no event, because the WS mux poll task (crates/forge-adapters/src/websocket/mux/poll.rs:28-37) dispatches _platform::subscriptions::poll as the subscriber (anonymous, no platform:read), where SSE drains with drain_identity (sse.rs:496-505). The plan now carries a forge-runtime fix: the mux by-id poll, resume and close use the same drain identity, confined to subscription ids this socket opened, and that test fails before the fix

gaps.note: Diffed the scaffolded tree (forge-runtime f8fa258f: tests/realtime_anon_subscribe.rs, 5 tests on notes_locked/notes_public over WS mux and SSE, plus the mux drain-identity fix and resume confinement; forge-portal-e2e edde8ae: P2.2 and the SSE anon-refusal spec retargeted to probe_locked, pinning UNAUTHENTICATED and 401) against intent revision 1 and its three acceptance criteria. Private-table refusal over both transports (WS error frame UNAUTHENTICATED never subscribed; SSE 401 + Bearer challenge, not text/event-stream): covered and green. Anon-readable literal-predicate table streams over both transports: covered and green (WS half needed the drain-identity fix the plan-boundary review already recorded as fixed). e2e specs target a private table, red before on the dev stack (subscribed; 200 text/event-stream) and green after, output verbatim in the step evidence. Subscribe and command keep the caller identity; no gap found.

Diffed the built lanes (forge-runtime step-ip1 f8fa258f vs its base 10195fb0: sse.rs drain_identity made pub(crate), mux poll.rs/handlers.rs/socket.rs drain as it, resume map check, tests/realtime_anon_subscribe.rs; forge-portal-e2e step-ip1 edde8ae vs main 3917e43: two specs on probe_locked) against intent revision 1 statement and its acceptance. statement: An anonymous realtime subscribe (WebSocket mux subscribe frame, or GET /api/v1/data/{table}/subscribe over SSE) to a table whose read policy does not admit anonymous callers is refused at subscribe time (WS: error frame, never subscribed; SSE: 401 with Bearer challenge, no event stream), while an anonymous subscribe to a table whose select policy is a literal predicate still streams, matching the REST data API. The runtime already enforces this (forge-storage crud_emitter has_public_read_policy); the forge-portal-e2e reds come from PS-1 making probe_items public, so the specs move to the private probe_locked table and forge-runtime gains tests pinning both halves over both transports.
